chapter: England, later career and closing thoughts
title: Her usual Los Angeles sidemen
summary: She names regular bassists Billy Hadnott and Benny Booker, drummers Gene Washington and Al Bartee, and Lee Young on her first session.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: But here, here in Los Angeles, you usually work with the same two musicians, don't you?

Yes, I work with the same. Well, I work with either Billy Hadnott, who was on my very first record date, and he's still around, a very wonderful bass player. And then Benny Booker, who was the first bass player who went on the road with me. He went -- he was on the road with me about, I guess, a couple of years before -- before George Duvivier was

with me. George Duvivier went to Europe with me. Then I use -- right now I'm using a very fine drummer, Gene Washington. He's a very good drummer. And I have worked with -- I've worked with many drummers. Al Bartee and some of the other fine drummers around town. And, as I think I told you, Lee Young was on my first record session. He was on the, "Hurry On Down," session. At that time he was a playing musician. But now he's an executive, now.
At Motown Records, yes. So he has come a long way.
